title: An unquoted `git diff -U0` hunk-header parse under `set -u` crashes on a one-line hunk, not on hunk content
content:
Recorded from #21 (merged to main as cab267f) for any future QA battery cell that parses `git diff -U0` hunk headers, because this is a generic bash-word-splitting bug that will recur in the next battery that tries the same shape of check, not a one-off in this run's cell. `verify-21.sh`'s AC15b cell parsed each `git diff -U0` hunk header of the form `@@ -<old_start>[,<old_count>] +<new_start>[,<new_count>] @@` with `a=$(sed -E 's/^@@ -([0-9]+)(,[0-9]+)? \+([0-9]+)(,[0-9]+)? @@.*/\1 \2 \3 \4/')` followed by an UNQUOTED `set -- $a`. git OMITS the `,<count>` group entirely when a hunk is exactly one line on that side (rendering `@@ -125 +125 @@` rather than `@@ -125,1 +125,1 @@`), so the sed capture leaves two of the four groups empty, and the unquoted `set --` word-splits the empty fields away, leaving only TWO positionals instead of four. Under `set -uo pipefail` (the mode this battery, and most careful ones, run under), the reference to `$3` for the new-hunk start line is then a `TypeError`-equivalent bash 'unbound variable' that terminates the ENTIRE script at that cell -- every later cell (AC16, AC17, and this battery's D-series) never runs at all, and a script that dies mid-run reads exactly like a smaller, passing battery unless the operator checks the cell count against the expected total.

MEASURED, FOUR HEADER SHAPES (the failure is a function of HUNK SHAPE, not diff content): `@@ -125,2 +125,3 @@` (both sides multi-line) parses correctly, 4 fields; `@@ -126,0 +127,1 @@` (a pure insertion) parses correctly, 4 fields; `@@ -125 +125,3 @@` (old side one-line, new side multi-line) parses to 3 fields and is SILENTLY WRONG (the old-count field absorbs the '+125,3' text under word-splitting) -- worse than the crash, because it produces a wrong answer with no error; `@@ -125 +125 @@` (both sides exactly one line) parses to 2 fields and CRASHES under `set -u`. A hunk confined to a single physical line on BOTH sides -- which is exactly what a design that puts several edits on one line (a common shape for a one-line prose or config edit) produces -- hits the worst case.

FIX, APPLIED BY QA AT #21 PHASE 4 (three lines, semantics unchanged for the shapes that already worked): change the sed replacement to `\1 x\2 \3 x\4` (an `x` PREFIX on the two optional count groups, so an EMPTY optional group becomes the literal string `x` rather than disappearing under word-splitting), then after `set -- $a`, read `ol="$1" oc="${2#x}" nl="$3" nc="${4#x}"`, strip a leading comma (`oc="${oc#,}"`; `nc="${nc#,}"`), and default an empty count to 1 (`oc="${oc:-1}"`; `nc="${nc:-1}"`) since git's own header convention is that an omitted count means exactly 1.

GENERALIZATION FOR THE NEXT BATTERY AUTHOR: never parse an optional regex-capture group with an unquoted `set --`/word-splitting shell idiom; either quote every expansion (`set -- "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4"` still loses positional COUNT information the same way, so quoting alone does not fix this) or, as done here, make an empty optional group survive as a non-empty sentinel before splitting. Add a control fixture with a one-line-both-sides hunk (the shape a single-physical-line edit produces) to any battery cell that walks `git diff -U0` hunk headers, before trusting it against a real diff; QA's own repair added exactly that as `AC15b.parser-oracle`, exercising the isolated parser over four header shapes it must read correctly and two it must refuse.
